newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Ex-Moscow air cargo rates firm, market volume stable.
newsitem.headline: Ex-Moscow air cargo rates firm, market volume stable.

text.p: Air cargo rates from Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport rose in the last three weeks, but the market was very stable, a Reuters survey showed.

Average rates to Frankfurt, London and Luxembourg from Russia's leading air cargo gateway rose five cents to $1.13 from $1.08, to $1.20 from $1.15 and to $1.35 from $1.30 per kilo for a 100 kg shipment respectively.
Igor Mordvinov, senior sales manager of Burlington Air Express Moscow, told Reuters airlines had increased their cargo rates by about five percent in recent weeks.
"The leader in this process is British Airways which has announced a sharp increase in rates to its Western European destinations," he said.

Mordvinov said that according to BA's plans, its rates per kg for a 100 kg direct shipment would be increased to $2.05 from $1.35 to Frankfurt and to $2.00 from $1.25 to Luxemburg. Rates on Moscow-London route would not be changed from $1.90, he said.
An official at British Airways' Moscow office said new rates would apply from January 20. He gave no more details.
Mordvinov said BA's rates from Moscow to Western Europe were attractive for many clients, but the increase could force many of them to find new carriers.
"We do not plan to increase our rates following BA...We will make shipments using other airlines instead of the British carrier," he said.
BA's decision would have a negative influence on the ex-Moscow air cargo market.
"High rates can seriously hit the market which is very competitive now," Mordvinov said.
Peter Vins, president of Vinlund Air, said the market was very active this week following a post-New Year lull.
"Many airlines, including Air France, increased their air cargo rates on average by 10-15 percent...and we are already feeling it," Vins said.
He warned that BA could lose many clients in Russia because of the sharp increase in rates.

Vladimir Pavlov, a Soby forwarder official, said Aeroflot planned to join foreign airlines in imposing a 10 percent fuel surcharge in February. "We are expecting a general rates increase soon," Pavlov said.
But Ilya Maslennikov, an official at the Eruslan forwarder firm, said some Yeltsin's health problems this month had caused concern among some clients.
"They phoned us asking firm guarantees for their shipments," he said.
Maslennikov also said forwarders had met serious problems with customs delivering transit cargoes through Sheremetyevo airport in recent weeks.
"Almost all forwarders at Sheremetyevo have problems with customs," he said.

"Our company had 15-20 tonnes of cargo turnover a week a few months ago, but now we have zero turnover," he said, adding that clients prefered to deliver cargoes with Western airlines directly to their final destination on Russian territory.

But Nikolai Belyaev, sales manager of EMS Garant Post, a forwarder for Air France, KLM and ANA Cargo, said the market had ignored Yeltsin's pneumonia, which put him in hospital last Wednesday. "The market feels fine," he said.
Sergey Mochalov, senior cargo manager at Aeroflot agent TCT Cargo, said the market was active in spite of New Year holidays.
"We have already felt BA's new cargo rates...But it is not clear how they can influence the market," he said.
Mochalov said the market would be sluggish in coming weeks due to possible customs rules changes. "Clients are waiting to see how the customs policy will change," he said.
A Transaero cargo official said clients were unable to comply with many customs rules for transit cargoes at Sheremetyevo airport. "We also suffer from this," he added.
Nadezda Sokolova, a cargo manager for Aeroservice forwarder firm said there were fewer orders in the first two weeks of January compared to the last two weeks of December.
"We hope February will be more active this month," she said, adding that BA clients were not hurrying to change carriers.
Meanwhile, rates to three key U.S. destinations -- Miami, New York and San Francisco -- rose four, three and three cents respectively.
Vins said shipments to U.S. destinations were very stable this month. "About 60 percent of our shipments were to the United States," he said.
Belyaev said traffic to North America and Western Euurope was stable in the last two weeks. "We also had good import deliveries before the New Year and Russian Chrismas" he said.
Mordvinov said Burlington Air Express Moscow planned many shipments to Rio de Janeiro, Buenos Aires and Peru in the next few months.
"We also hope to have stable shipments to India and China, he added.
Sokolova said there was a big demand for shipments from Moscow to Bejing, but Aeroflot did not operate its freighters on this route due to weak shipments from there.
"One of our clients made a shipment to this destination by rail-road, wasting a lot of time," she said. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
